name: Cetuximab plus concurrent radiation (Bonner regimen)
disease: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

biomarkers.note: Cetuximab is an anti-EGFR antibody; EGFR is highly expressed in most head and neck squamous cell carcinomas. p16/HPV status is prognostic but not a dose gate. Note: in p16-positive (HPV-associated) oropharyngeal cancer, RTOG 1016 and De-ESCALATE showed cetuximab-RT was INFERIOR to cisplatin-RT; cetuximab-RT is used mainly for cisplatin-ineligible patients based on the Bonner trial (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) 2.2026; DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 23, lines 58117 to 58121 and 62062).

lineOfTherapy: concurrent bioradiation for locoregionally advanced SCCHN, principally for patients who are not candidates for cisplatin; not line-scoped

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: locoregionally advanced SCCHN treated with definitive radiation, typically in cisplatin-ineligible patients
eligibilityCriteria.locator: Chapter 23, lines 58117 to 58121 (cetuximab concomitant with radiation improved locoregional control, PFS, OS versus radiation alone, Bonner); line 62079 (cetuximab option per Bonner for non-cisplatin candidates)

drugs.name: Cetuximab (loading dose)
drugs.route: IV, week 1 (loading), given approximately 1 week before starting radiation

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 98801 (cetuximab 400 mg/m2 week 1 followed by 250 mg/m2 weekly); line 124823 (cetuximab 400 mg/m2 loading dose)

drugs.notes: Source: cetuximab 400 mg/m2 IV loading dose in week 1 (DeVita 12th ed., lines 98801 and 124823). Bonner regimen loading dose given about 1 week before radiation begins. Premedicate with an H1 antihistamine; monitor for infusion reaction.

drugs.name: Cetuximab (weekly maintenance)

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 98801 (400 mg/m2 week 1 followed by 250 mg/m2 weekly); Chapter 23 line 62062 (cetuximab 250 mg per m2)

drugs.notes: Source: cetuximab 250 mg/m2 IV weekly following the loading dose (DeVita 12th ed., line 98801; Chapter 23 line 62062). Weekly during the radiation course; number of weekly doses runs with the radiation schedule and is not fixed by the cited source (see verifyFields). Monitor for acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion reactions.

premedications.name: Antihistamine premedication
premedications.notes: H1 antihistamine before cetuximab, especially the loading dose, to reduce infusion-reaction risk.

supportiveCare: Infusion-reaction precautions with cetuximab (higher risk with the loading dose).
Skin care for acneiform rash; monitor and replete magnesium (cetuximab hypomagnesemia).
Cetuximab is minimally emetogenic; antiemetic prophylaxis is not routinely required for the antibody itself.

monitoring: Infusion-reaction monitoring during and after each cetuximab dose
Mucositis / radiation dermatitis during concurrent RT

doseModificationRules.text: Stop infusion; manage reaction. Grade 3 to 4 reactions generally require permanent discontinuation. Physician decides.
Review required; interrupt and consider dose modification per labeling. Physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 98801 (cetuximab 400 mg/m2 week 1 then 250 mg/m2 weekly), line 124823 (400 mg/m2 loading), Chapter 23 lines 58117 to 58121 (Bonner cetuximab-RT phase III) and line 62062 (250 mg per m2; RTOG 1016 / De-ESCALATE context)

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
guideline.locator: Cetuximab listed as a concurrent systemic therapy option (algorithm line 6175, category 2B); exact loading/weekly numeric doses are not tabulated in the provided guideline pages, so numeric grounding is taken from DeVita core

sources.name: Bonner trial (via DeVita 12th ed. core)
sources.value: Cetuximab-RT improves locoregional control, PFS, and OS versus RT alone

sources.name: RTOG 1016 / De-ESCALATE (via DeVita 12th ed. and Standard Guidelines (NCCN))
sources.value: Cetuximab-RT is inferior to cisplatin-RT in p16-positive oropharyngeal cancer

divergence.note: Cetuximab-RT is a valid bioradiation option (Bonner) but is inferior to high-dose cisplatin-RT in p16-positive oropharyngeal cancer; it is used chiefly for cisplatin-ineligible patients. Patient selection left to clinical review.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for Cetuximab plus concurrent radiation (Bonner regimen), an anti-EGFR bioradiation option for locoregionally advanced SCCHN, principally for cisplatin-ineligible patients. Sites served (squamous histology): oral cavity (#32), tongue (#33), lip (#34), oropharyngeal (#35), HPV-positive oropharyngeal (#36, p16/HPV prognostic only, and note cetuximab-RT is inferior to cisplatin-RT here), hypopharyngeal (#38), laryngeal (#39), sinonasal (#41); nasopharyngeal (#37) and salivary (#40) are not covered by this protocol. Doses fully grounded: Cetuximab 400 mg/m2 IV loading in week 1 then 250 mg/m2 IV weekly (DeVita 12th ed. lines 98801 and 124823; Chapter 23 lines 58117 to 58121 and 62062). basis bsa (mg/m2), consistent with the source. The number of weekly maintenance doses runs with the radiation course and is not fixed by the cited source, so regimen.cycles is set to VERIFY. A divergence records that cetuximab-RT is inferior to cisplatin-RT in p16-positive oropharyngeal cancer. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
